goal: Number abbreviation for leaderboards with rounding carry across suffixes and no negative zero
prompt: In my Roblox game: my leaderboard shows huge numbers. Write a --!strict pure Luau function `abbreviate(n: number): string`. Suffixes: K (thousand), M (million), B (billion), T (trillion). Values below 1000 print as a whole number rounded to the nearest integer (half up). Larger values are divided by the unit and rounded to at most one decimal (half up) and the ".0" is dropped, so 1000 is "1K", 1500 is "1.5K", 12345 is "12.3K". If the rounding reaches 1000 in the current unit the next suffix is used instead: 999999 is "1M" (not "1000K") and 999.5 is "1K". T is the largest suffix, so 1500000000000000 is "1500T". Negative numbers get a leading "-" and use the same rules, but a number that rounds to zero prints "0" (never "-0"). NaN, infinity and non-numbers raise an error.
